intro_html: A Korean cookbook recipe: the cabbage is brined, salted for 12 hours under a weight, rinsed, then filled leaf by leaf from the middle out with a gochugaru filling and wrapped in its own outer leaves. Your additions go into the filling: dried baby anchovies and sakura shrimp chopped with a knife, and pear juice squeezed through cheesecloth.

mise.items_html: chopped anchovies · chopped shrimp · pear juice
mise.name: Your additions

mise.items_html: anchovy sauce · shrimp sauce · kelp stock · sugar
mise.name: Sauces + sugar

notes.html:
• Based on the recipe in Easy Korean Cooking (cookbook), with your additions: dried baby anchovies, sakura shrimp and pear juice.
  • The amounts of your additions are a starting guess — adjust them next batch.
If you can’t get salted anchovy or salted shrimp sauce, fish sauce stands in for either — but the Korean versions are worth hunting down.
notes.title_html: Fish sauce instead of the Korean sauces

notes.html: Use coarse salt for both the brine and the leaves — fine table salt is saltier by volume and lands unevenly.

steps.body_html:
• Stir 1 cup of coarse salt into 2 l of water in a bowl big enough to hold half a cabbage.
  • Peel off the outer leaves and keep them — they wrap the kimchi in step 6.
  • Cut the cabbage in half lengthwise and dunk the halves in the brine.

how.caption: Peel off the outer leaves and keep them — they wrap the kimchi at the end.
Cut the cabbage in half lengthwise.
Dunk the halves in the brine.

steps.title: Brine and halve

steps.body_html:
• Take the halves out and work the second cup of coarse salt in between the leaves, mostly onto the thick white stems.
  • Leave them cut faces up for 7 hours (12 in winter), then flip them face down for 5 hours more.
  • Keep weight on them throughout — a heavy plate or board, or a bag of water — so the salt gets in evenly.

how.caption: Lift the leaves and sprinkle coarse salt between them, mostly on the thick white stems.
Press them under a heavy plate — 7 hours cut-side up, then 5 hours cut-side down.

steps.title: Salt and press

steps.body_html:
• Wash the salt off under cold water, opening the leaves so it reaches inside.
  • Stand the halves in a colander and let them drip for about an hour.

how.caption: Rinse thoroughly in cold water, opening the leaves.

steps.title: Rinse and drain

steps.body_html:
• Slice the daikon into thin 0.3 cm matchsticks; cut the green onions into 3 cm pieces.
  • Your additions — chop finely with a knife:
    • dried baby anchovies a small handful (~10 g) — enough to taste a little
    • dried sakura shrimp a small handful (~5–10 g) — the same idea
  • Crush or grate the garlic — a ceramic grater is best, a fine metal one works too.
  • Grate the ginger and squeeze it through cheesecloth for the ginger juice.
  • Grate the Asian pear, put it in cheesecloth and squeeze out the juice — the juice is what you want.

how.caption: Daikon: slice into thin 3 mm planks.
Stack a few planks and cut them into 0.3 cm matchsticks.
Green onions: line them up and cut into 3 cm lengths.
Your additions: chop the dried anchovies and shrimp finely with a knife.
Grate the garlic and ginger on a ceramic grater, rubbing in small circles.
Squeeze the grated pear (and ginger) through cheesecloth — the juice is what you want.

steps.title: Prepare the filling

steps.body_html:
• Gloves on. Mix everything from step 4 with:
    • gochugaru (Korean chilli powder) 1 cup (200 ml)
    • salted anchovy sauce 100 ml
    • salted shrimp sauce 3 tbsp
    • sugar 4 tbsp
    • kelp (kombu) stock 100 ml
  • Let it stand about 30 minutes so the flavours come together.

how.caption: Gloves on: mix the gochugaru, sauces, sugar and stock with everything from step 4.

steps.title: Mix the filling

steps.body_html:
• Start at the middle: lift the innermost leaf next to the core and smear filling over it right down to the core.
  • Lay it back, lift the next leaf out from the middle and repeat — work outward until every leaf is coated.
  • Fold the outer leaves you saved around each half like a parcel, so none of the filling escapes.
  • Press the parcels into an airtight jar and give them 5–7 days in the fridge before eating.

how.caption: Start at the middle: lift the innermost leaf and smear filling down to the core.
Lay it back, lift the next leaf out from the middle, repeat.
Work outward until the outer leaves are done.
Wrap each half in the outer leaves you kept.
Pack tightly into an airtight jar, then 5–7 days in the fridge.

steps.title: Fill, wrap and pack

timeline.note_html: In winter the first salting is 12 h instead of 7 h. Then 5–7 days in the fridge before serving.
